gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two labs that actually measure battery disagree on the Sony-vs-Bose order: RTINGS (Test Bench 2.3) measured the Bose QC Ultra 2nd Gen at 37 h and the Sony WH-1000XM6 at 31.75 h, while SoundGuys' 75 dB SPL rundown measured the Sony at 37 h 14 min and the Bose at 27 h 12 min; and the only one of the four picks with a published measured ANC figure is the AirPods Max 2 at 89.4% perceived-loudness attenuation (SoundGuys), the top noise-cancelling lab score of the four (9.0/10 vs 8.7 for Sony and Bose).
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages plus the What Hi-Fi best list. SoundGuys' cited compare page already gives SoundGuys battery (Sony 37.23 h, Bose 27.2 h), weights (254 g / 250 g) and NC scores (8.7 / 8.7), so the SoundGuys side alone is not new. The What Hi-Fi versus page and best list contain zero lab measurements (no dB, no measured hours; 30 h figures are maker claims). SoundGuys' cited best list names AirPods Max 2 for 'noise attenuation' but gives no figure. No cited or uncited result shows the RTINGS measured battery numbers (RTINGS compare pages in the results have those fields locked), the 89.4% AirPods Max 2 attenuation, the Momentum 4 measured 56–62 h, or the side-by-side MDAQS sound scores. RTINGS dB attenuation is paywalled, so the angle cannot settle Sony vs Bose ANC outright, which keeps this at 2 rather than 3.
decides: Confirms Sony vs Bose is a tie on noise cancelling (same 8.7/10 at SoundGuys; SoundGuys' head-to-head says no clear advantage) and removes battery as the tiebreaker ChatGPT implied: each lab puts a different one ahead, so the shopper should pick on comfort, sound or price, not runtime. It also tightens ChatGPT's Apple pick: AirPods Max 2 has the highest measured ANC of the four (89.4%, SoundGuys NC 9.0 'beats 98%') but is 386 g and measured only 21–22 h, so it is the pick for maximum attenuation, not just for Apple users. For Sennheiser Momentum 4, measured 56 h 21 min (SoundGuys) and 62.3 h (RTINGS) confirm the 60 h claim, while SoundGuys' 7.6/10 'below avg' noise-cancelling score and 'about 75%' low-frequency reduction quantify the ANC trade-off.
